core_obligations: Record base-change stability and Zariski locality of separatedness (proof lines 5804-5808).
Reduce to a flat surjective morphism of affines and interpret separatedness of f' as Delta' being a closed immersion, hence universally closed (proof lines 5809-5814).
Identify Delta' as the base change of Delta : X -> X x_S X along S' -> S (proof lines 5815-5816).
Use descent of universal closedness to get Delta universally closed, then a closed immersion because it is an immersion, and conclude (proof lines 5816-5822).
proof_roadmap: Separatedness as closedness of the diagonal (proof lines 5809-5814).
The diagonal as a base change (proof lines 5815-5816).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property 'f is separated' is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5797-5801). The proof records base-change stability and Zariski locality, then reduces to a flat surjective morphism of affines with separated base change f': separatedness of f' says that the diagonal Delta' is a closed immersion, hence universally closed; the key observation is that Delta' is the base change of Delta : X -> X x_S X along S' -> S, so descent of universal closedness makes Delta universally closed; since Delta is an immersion, a universally closed immersion is a closed immersion, and f is separated; the general locality lemma concludes (proof lines 5803-5822). The level is H3: the reduction of separatedness to a property of the diagonal and the identification of that diagonal with a base change are both displayed, and the passage from universally closed immersion to closed immersion is the pointed step.
